column1: # comment: "Cross-cutting attestation alignments. PROV-O is the strongest RDF alignment (Activity, Entity, wasAttributedTo). W3C VC/DID is partially aligned where the RDF vocabulary is stable. Supply-chain formats (in-toto, SLSA, DSSE, Sigstore, SCITT, C2PA, RATS/EAT) and blockchain identifiers (CAIP, EIP) have no canonical RDF vocabularies; mappings are loose or refused and documented here."
# # Loose / refused mappings (no canonical RDF vocabulary available):

column6: no public SCITT RDF vocabulary at time of writing
loose — nanopub RDF exists but the signed-graph pattern is implementation-specific
CAIP-10 / did:pkh alignment — identifier scheme, not RDF class
An attestation is a kind of provenance entity — information object that participates in an activity and may be attributed to an agent
A VC is credential-like; Attestation is broader (includes non-credential envelopes such as SLSA, DSSE, transparency logs)
WoT Endorsement is a key-certification edge; Attestation is the broader envelope pattern. Certification (trust.ttl) is the closer match.
An attestation artifact is a provenance entity
Verification and quality assessment are distinct but related; quality may consume verification results as evidence
A verification result is the outcome of checking a VC, not the presentation itself; loose mapping
The attester is the agent to whom the attestation is attributed; directionality differs (attester is a direct property, wasAttributedTo is an annotation/derivation)
